messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] scantwo permutation with multiple phenotype
messages.body_plain:
It should be the case that the function calc.penalties() will work on the scantwo permutation results even if they have multiple columns.  If you want the penalties for just the first phenotype, you pull out the first row from the output

  allpen <- calc.penalties(perm35_50.2)
  thepen1 <- allpen[1,]

Alternatively, you can pull out the first column from each component of the scantwo permutations results, though you then need to re-do the "class"...something like the following:

  perm35_50.2_sqrt35Hz <- lapply(perm35_50.2, function(a) a[,1,drop=FALSE])
  class(perm35_50.2_sqrt35Hz) <- class(perm35_50.2)

karl

messages.subject: discrepancy between summary and plot
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
We're using CIM for analysing RI data. We get the following output
                             chr  pos   lod
c1.loc315                      1  315  1.36
an10538.10b.T.58_2L_19786704   2  984 10.10
an12072.06b.G.58_3R_26622579   3 2126  3.02

When we plot the LOD curve, additional peak with a LOD ~ 3.8 appears
on Ch 2. Why wasn't this QTL reported in the summary (two QTL with a
lower LOD were reported)? Is this QTL real? (the permutation 5% level
is 3.32). If it is spurious, how can we get rid of it from the plot?

Many thanks, Eran
